findings.falsifier: a review_coverage re-run that counts any of these files without a wrapper, or an audit-lead rebind proving the intent reading wrong for a specific file.
findings.finding: The controller gate scan undercounts real, hash-pinned, full-schema accepts because two review-encoding families are unreadable to it: (a) nested `verdicts[]` with `targets[]` (reviews/L0-review-032.json: L0 and L1 accepts at ce42d205e761 / 315c19145065), and (b) `target_id: "path#sha256"` with a matching reviewed_sha256 (reviews/F2b-review-worker-001.json: F2b accept at 1bb78ce9b357). A third, scoped family is also invisible and must stay excluded from full-schema credit by design: reviews/F0F1-softflag-disposition-review.json (astra-lead-audit) carries the F0/F1 soft-flag dispositions as nested accepts with counts_as_full_schema_verdict=false. The audit lead's reviews/A1-rebind-coverage.json is an adjudication census that restates other reviewers' verdicts, not a source of the lead's own accepts (excluded by construction here). The per-node delta and the minimal non-semantic wrapper repair are in `intent_delta`; rebinding is owned by the audit lead / controller, not by this worker.
findings.impact: L0 would reach two distinct full accepts (worker-011 counted + worker-032 intent); F2b already has two counted (deepseek-flash-17, worker-030) and would reach three. The F0/F1 soft-flag dispositions are recorded but cannot be credited by the scan as written.

findings.falsifier: an F1 accept file that binds to 9a8bd4c96800 under the controller rule.
findings.finding: F1 has zero accepts at any encoding at measured hash 9a8bd4c96800: the bound F1 verdict mix is {"revise": 1}, with 17 further F1 files pinned to superseded hashes. The G-FORM F1 criterion is content-blocked, not binding-blocked; the next second-review effort should go to F1 content, not to rebinding.
findings.impact: G-FORM cannot pass on F1 until an accept exists at the measured hash.

The counted matrix is the gate-relevant one; the intent column is what a tolerant parser plus audit-lead rebind would see. G-F0's only stale-encoded accept is reviews/F0-review-lead-audit.json at superseded 565a6e505188.
findings.impact: Gives the next lifecycle pass the exact accept deficit per gate.

findings.falsifier: a parser change that binds all three families and a re-run showing zero invisible accepts.
findings.finding: Encoding-family census: 5 file(s) use `path#sha256` target ids (['F0-rev26-adjudication-090.json', 'F1-review-025.json', 'F2b-review-worker-001.json', 'L0-review-19.json', 'L0-review-worker-001.json']), 9 file(s) carry nested accept blocks (['A1-rebind-coverage.json', 'A1-rebind-coverage.prev-20260912T0025.json', 'F2a-review-lead-audit.json', 'F2b-review-07.json', 'G-NUM-protocol-review-rev1-advisory.json', 'G-NUM-protocol-review.json', 'L0-review-032.json', 'L1-spotcheck-09.json', 'convergence-18.json']), and the NO_TOP_LEVEL_VERDICT family has 7 file(s). These are reasonable authoring choices that silently lose gate credit under the current one-format parser.
findings.impact: Suggests a tolerant target/verdict parser (or a wrapper convention) to stop losing verdicts.

findings.finding: The corpus is live. Within the W021-BIND-01 work window, reviews/L0-review-worker-006.json changed verdict (accept -> revise, observed 00:23 -> 00:25) and reviews/F0-review-094.json changed verdict (accept -> revise, mtime 00:29), moving the counted F0 accept set from [worker-094] to [] between two runs of this same script. Every count here is snapshot-pinned per file; the report voids itself on any recorded file-hash drift (per-file drift for this run is recorded in `input_drift`).

findings.falsifier: a re-measured L0 hash equal to ce42d205e761, or a review binding at the new hash.
findings.finding: L0 was rewritten during the audit window: ledger/theorems.jsonl moved ce42d205e761 -> 3e3d35531421 measured 3e3d35531421 vs the pass-02 frozen ce42d205e761 (140547 bytes -> 166415 bytes), and the row status vocabulary changed accepted(50) -> included_unreviewed(50) with new supports_claim_basis / review_status / acceptance_authority fields. Consequence: 10 L0 review file(s) (['L0-review-011.json', 'L0-review-17.json', 'L0-review-18-current.json', 'L0-review-19.json', 'L0-review-21.json', 'L0-review-22.json', 'L0-review-lead-audit-r2.json', 'L0-review-lead-audit.json', 'L0-review-worker-001.json', 'L0-review-worker-006-superseded-ce42d205.json']) pin the superseded hash, so zero L0 verdicts bind at the new revision and G-LIT's L0 criterion restarts at the new hash (superseded-hash verdicts are advisory only, astra_lifecycle.py:295-296). Any L0 accept counted at ce42d205e761 in earlier gate reasons is void pending re-review at the new revision.
findings.impact: G-LIT L0 review credit resets; the status downgrade does resolve the self-certified-acceptance objection on its face, which is reviewable at the new hash.

findings.falsifier: a re-measure showing the four artifacts still at their 00:21:55 hashes, or a gate reason that binds a pre-00:32 verdict at the current bytes.
findings.finding: Mid-window republication voided the standing review corpus. Relative to the controller gate audit at 00:21:55, 5 artifact(s) moved: F0 276009f4f63d->0abb9ed8a961 (research_map/formulation_taxonomy.yaml, mtime 2026-09-12T00:31:41+08:00); F1 9a8bd4c96800->cce9c60146d6 (schemas/af_wcc_vacuum.yaml, mtime 2026-09-12T00:32:02+08:00); F2a b6123750b37d->5476a3f2c6bc (schemas/af_scc_c2_vacuum.yaml, mtime 2026-09-12T00:32:02+08:00); F2b 1bb78ce9b357->55d0a1ea9bda (schemas/af_scc_c0_vacuum.yaml, mtime 2026-09-12T00:32:02+08:00); L0 ce42d205e761->3e3d35531421 (ledger/theorems.jsonl, mtime 2026-09-12T00:30:49+08:00). At snapshot 2026-09-12T00:33:18+08:00 the counted full-schema accept sets are {"L0": ["worker-006"]} (empty for 7 of 8 nodes), and 72 review file(s) pin a superseded hash. Per protocol any verdict bound to superseded bytes is advisory only, so every pre-republication gate reason and every accept counted before ~00:32 must be treated as void until re-issued at the measured hashes.
findings.impact: Explains the zero-accept matrix without needing new content defects: review throughput is being outrun by republication. The next lifecycle pass must re-pin and re-scan, and review effort should be scheduled against a frozen revision.
